event.title: Going for Baroque
event.description: Going for Baroque is a weekly series of mini-recitals at the Memorial Art Gallery. It is offered each Sunday at 1:30 pm and again at 3:00 pm. It offers the opportunity for students from the Eastman School of Music to perform alongside professional musicians on the Italian Baroque organ on the second floor of the museum. The 25-minute mini-recital is included with museum admission. Owned by the Eastman School of Music, the fully restored Italian Baroque organ is the only full-size antique Italian organ in North America. The organ is the centerpiece of an installation that highlights more than 30 major Baroque-period paintings and sculptures.

event.title: Mindful MAGiC: Candlelit Consciousness Concert
event.description: Ignite your inner calm with an evening of sound and shadow! October 8th, step out of the daily rush and into the glow. Mindful MAGiC: Candlelit Consciousness Concert invites you to experience our auditorium as never before—filled with gongs and transformed into a flickering sanctuary of over 200 candles. Harold Taddy brings the sound bath element of MAG’s celebrated wellness series to the main stage, weaving a tapestry of tranquil soundscapes. To help guide your journey, this performance features poetic guided meditations by spoken word artist Theo Trombulak woven seamlessly throughout the experience, creating a space that is as intellectually stirring as it is restorative. Part recital and part immersive meditation, this is a rare opportunity to experience “concert-style” mindfulness in a supportive, beautifully lit environment. This is a seated experience—just bring yourself. Less movement, more MAGiC—just you and the sound. Important Program Details All guests must be seated by 6:30 pm to preserve the tranquil nature of the session. To ensure a peaceful atmosphere for all participants, late entry will not be permitted once the session is underway. Food and beverages are not permitted in the galleries. Please use the designated cubby spaces in the Vanden Brul Pavilion for storage. This is a seated experience in MAG’s auditorium. Seating is arranged in a theater-style configuration, offering clear views of the stage and excellent sound quality throughout the venue. Guests may choose their seats upon arrival on a first-come, first-served basis. For added comfort, feel free to bring a blanket and settle in for the experience. For questions about this program, contact Katie Nguyen, Senior Manager of Guest Services, at knguyen@mag.rochester.edu. Ticket sales end on Thursday, October 8, at 6:15 pm. Ticket includes museum admission. Member discount applies to the first two tickets in your order.

event.title: Museum of the Dead
event.description: Do you like scary movies? Museum of the Dead is back with all your favorite (slightly) scary experiences—art, music, a costume contest, cocktails, fortune-telling, and food—it’s the party you cannot miss! Sign up early for your chance to save on tickets to get in on more activities, more friends, more fun, more giveaways, and more scares this year. Ticket sales are open for everyone! There’s a $10 discount on general tickets through October 1 (applied at checkout). Buy general tickets VIP Experience—SOLD OUT! Want the ultimate Museum of the Dead experience? MAG’s VIP hour is back! Your ticket includes exclusive Scream-tastic swag, entry to the VIP lounge (with dedicated bar), a discounted ticket to the food trucks, a complimentary drink, and a VIP photo op. You’ll also be able to register for tarot card readings and ghost tours during the VIP hour, as well as a few spots during the rest of the night. Tarot Card Reading & Ghost Tours Timed-ticket alert! Be sure to sign up ahead of time to secure a time slot with our fortune-tellers or a ghost tour with Monroe County Paranormal Investigations. (There’s no additional cost to reserving a spot for a reading or a tour, but space for both is limited.) The links to register are shared in the confirmation email sent when you buy tickets. Please note that the registrations links for VIP guests are different from the links for general admission; please use the links provided. Schedule of Events 7:00–8:00 pm | VIP hour 7:00–11:00 pm | Food Trucks 8:00–10:00 pm | Museum Galleries open for exploration 8:15–9:45 pm | Tarot card reading (by registration) in Renaissance Gallery 8:30–10:00 pm | Organ concert in the Fountain Court 8:00–11:00 pm | Party in Cutler Union & Vanden Brul Pavilion 8:00–10:00 pm | Arts & Crafts in the M&T Bank Ballroom 8:00–11:00 pm | Movie: Scream, shown in the M&T Bank Ballroom 8:00–11:00 pm | Live DJ & Dancing, Step & Repeat Photo Op in the Vanden Brul Pavilion 10:00 pm | Costume Contest winners announced in the Vanden Brul Pavilion Costume Contest Throughout the night, MAG staff members will be giving out cards to guests who qualify for the costume contest. Save your card, and meet at the Admissions Desk/entrance to the galleries at 9:50 pm, with the costume contest at 10 pm. If YOU think you qualify for the contest, find a MAG staff member and let them know, they might just give you a card! At 10:00 pm, everyone will gather in the Vanden Brul Pavilion, and the DJ will announce the winners. Winners will get great prizes from local businesses! event.title: Art Lover’s Tour: Santa Fe
event.description: Join us in Georgia O’Keeffe country and delve into the rich heritage of northern New Mexico on a journey that weaves together centuries-old craft traditions with the splendor of iconic sights. Enjoy opportunities to engage directly with skilled local artisans, art curators, and gallery owners, whose insights reveal how ancestral knowledge, materials, and cultural values continue to shape living artistic traditions in the Southwest today. Visits to museums, Abiquiú, and Ghost Ranch situate artistic practice within the dramatic terrain that inspired generations of makers, painters, and writers. A visit to O’Keeffe’s studio reveals the deep connection between the artist and the creative vision she cultivated there for more than four decades. In Chimayo, examine the continuity of devotional art, weaving, and vernacular architecture rooted in centuries-old Hispano traditions. Throughout, enjoy Santa Fe’s cuisine defined by the use of heirloom ingredients and deeply rooted regional flavors that feel both ancient and inventive. To be added to the waitlist for this tour, contact Emily Whitson, Distant Horizons, at 562-983-8828 or emilyw@distant-horizons.com. Tour Highlights Enjoy a tour of the Georgia O’Keeffe Museum pairing iconic paintings with personal objects that illuminate her deep connection to the New Mexico landscape. Meet with gallery owner Andrea Fisher, a premier authority on New Mexico Pueblo pottery who maintains close relationships with artists. Go behind-the-scenes at the Museum of International Folk Art with Laura Addison, one of the world’s largest museums dedicated to folk art. Basketry was one of the first craft forms practiced by Indigenous communities and learn about the various styles at the Adobe Gallery. Be part of a curated visit to O’Keefe’s home at Abiquiú, and understand how the landscape inspired her with a visit to nearby Ghost Ranch. Visit Evoke Gallery and meet with director Katherine Erickson. Evoke emphasizes contemporary figurative painting and representational art. Visit the IAIA’s Museum of Contemporary Native Arts and be joined by Manuela Well Off Man, chief curator for a very special visit. Explore the Santuario de Chimayo, the second most important Catholic pilgrimage center in the United States. Accompanied by Patricia Trujillo-Oviedo learn about the weaving traditions of Chimayo. She is a seventh generation descendant of original local settlers. Throughout the program, enjoy Santa Fe’s cuisine and deeply rooted regional flavors that feel are both ancient and inventive. New Mexico blends Native American, Hispanic, and Anglo traditions in dishes that celebrate locally grown ingredients. event.title: Chasing Rainbows: How We Talk About Color
event.description: Color is one of the most foundational experiences we have as humans—yet our understanding about what color is, how we experience it, and how to talk about it is a bit squishy. Is aqua blue or green (or neither)? Does that change when you put aqua next to a blue or green? And if it does change, does that mean it’s still aqua? Science can provide answers—but what happens when the answers science gives us contradict our own experiences? Even artists who work with color all the time sometimes struggle with how to order, describe, and work with color. Is there a common language we can all use? Join lexicographer and author Kory Stamper as she guides you through a kaleidoscopic journey through modern color science, color psychology, color naming and descriptions, and our perceptions about color using artworks in the MAG collection. Kory Stamper is an author and lexicographer who has spent near 30 years thinking (too deeply) about how to define the words that define us. In her 20 years as an editor at Merriam-Webster, she defined everything from “blue plate special” to “god” and answered dictionary user questions on everything from what color “nude” really is to why it’s “toothpaste” and not “teethpaste.” She has written about her time as a dictionary writer in Word by Word: The Secret Life of Dictionaries (2017, Pantheon). Her moderate obsession with color began during her time at Merriam-Webster, and led to her second nonfiction book, True Color: The Strange and Spectacular Quest to Define Color—from Azure to Zinc Pink (2026, Knopf). Lecture will be followed by a book signing in the Vanden Brul Pavilion until 8:30 pm. event.title: Mindful MAGiC: Sonic Yoga
event.description: Begin your morning with a restorative experience that blends mindful movement and immersive sound for a powerful journey inward. Set in the serene surroundings of the Fountain Court, this special session features yoga and meditation led by Shanna Pagan and is accompanied by an immersive live soundscape from Harold Taddy (The Gong Situation). What You Can Bring Yoga mat, bolsters, and layers for comfort Cozy socks A water bottle with a secure, leak-proof lid (no straws) Important Arrival Details Doors open at 9:00 am Check-in at the Admissions Desk no later than 9:15 am to get situated Please arrive on time to preserve the tranquil nature of the session The session lasts 9:30–10:30 am, followed by a 15-minute courtesy window to ease your transition into the day. Museum admission begins at 11:00 am when the galleries open to the public. Come curious. Move with intention. Let the sound guide you. For questions about this program, contact Katie Nguyen, Senior Manager of Guest Services, at knguyen@mag.rochester.edu. Ticket sales end on Saturday, November 28, at 9:00 am. Ticket includes museum admission. Member discount applies to the first two tickets in your order.
